name: Spain
score_rationale: LAND stays 3: pasture and dryland at USD 3,700-8,100/ha, freehold open to foreigners, whole hamlets under EUR 100k; the Ley 8/1975 military permit only bites in coastal/border zones. VISA stays 2: golden visa gone, but NLV (EUR 2,400/mo), DNV (EUR 2,849/mo) and the autónomo permit are reliable per-person routes with PR at 5 years; no group route and 10-year citizenship. TAX stays 1: worldwide taxation at up to 47%, savings 19-30%, wealth tax plus a now-permanent solidarity tax above EUR 3M; Beckham helps only remote employees. LAW stays 3: a statutory communal-land co-op with tax privileges and strong co-op registries, offset by restrictive suelo rústico building rules. LIFE stays 3: HDI 0.918, Numbeo health 76.8, GPI rank 25, cheap rural living. STAB stays 2: solid EU/eurozone anchors but CPI at 55 and falling, WJP 0.71 mid-pack for the EU, and the highest drought exposure of any large EU state (ND-GAIN 61.0). Scores unchanged from the July 2026 record; evidence confirms them.
verdict: Best-in-class communal-land-co-op law and dirt-cheap interior land; the tax bill and 10-year citizenship are the drawbacks.
summary: Spain is the strongest EU option for a land-based commune on paper: interior dryland and pasture sells for roughly USD 3,700-8,000/ha, foreigners can buy freehold (non-EU buyers need a Defence Ministry permit only in listed coastal/border zones), and Ley 27/1999 contains a purpose-built 'cooperativa de explotación comunitaria de la tierra' with a 50% corporate-tax bonification. The catches are that the golden visa is gone (closed 3 April 2025), so each non-EU adult needs either EUR 2,400/month of passive income (non-lucrative, no work), EUR 2,849/month of foreign remote income (digital nomad) or a self-employed/entrepreneur permit, and that after 183 days you pay Spanish tax on worldwide income at up to 47% plus wealth/solidarity tax. Buy an existing hamlet (aldea) with legal dwellings rather than bare farmland: suelo rústico rules make building new homes on agricultural land slow and usually impossible beyond one farm-linked house per 0.5-2.5 ha parcel.

land.text: 'España vaciada' marginal land €1–6k/ha; productive €8–22k/ha
land.house: Griegos free plots (one family); buy an abandoned aldea directly
land.ownership_note: Foreign individuals and foreign-owned companies can own rural and agricultural land freehold with no residency, reciprocity, size-cap or local-company requirement. One exception: under Ley 8/1975 and RD 689/1978 (zones of interest for national defence) non-EU/non-Swiss nationals need prior Ministry of Defence authorisation to buy rural (not urban) land in designated zones - the Balearic and Canary Islands, Ceuta/Melilla, the French and Portuguese border strips, the Galician coast, the Cádiz coast, Murcia and southern Alicante. Authorisation takes 2-6 months and a notary will refuse to sign without it. Buying through a Spanish SL does not avoid the rule if the SL is majority non-EU owned. Interior 'España vaciada' land (Castilla y León, Aragón, Extremadura, Castilla-La Mancha, inland Andalucía) is outside these zones.
land.build_rules: Unidad mínima de cultivo (UMC) set per region blocks subdividing farmland below roughly 1 ha irrigated / several ha dryland. New housing on suelo rústico: Andalucía (Ley LISTA) requires 2.5 ha for an isolated non-farm dwelling, max 1% footprint, one house per parcel, 2 storeys/7 m, 100 m from other houses; Castilla y León allows a dwelling from 5,000 m2 with UMC usually 1 ha; most regions require the house to be tied to a working farm.
land.cheap_house_program: No state 'EUR 1 house' scheme. Whole abandoned hamlets (aldeas) are listed from about EUR 39,000, most under EUR 100,000 (106 listings in 2025, 31 in Galicia); Salto de Castro (Zamora) sold for EUR 310,000 in 2026. Village incentive schemes are small and family-targeted: Griegos (Teruel) offered 3 months' free rent then EUR 225/month plus a job (3,000 applicants); Ponga (Asturias) pays EUR 3,000 per couple plus EUR 3,000 per child; Rubiá (Ourense) EUR 100-150/month aid and EUR 50/month rentals; Valle del Ambroz (Cáceres) aid for remote workers.
land.note: MAPA 2024 survey (published Aug 2025): national average EUR 10,248/ha (+2.8%); cheapest regions Castilla y León EUR 5,115/ha and Aragón EUR 5,175/ha; by class pastizal EUR 3,279, dryland arable EUR 7,239, dryland nuts EUR 7,621, prados EUR 11,553, dryland olive EUR 13,063, irrigated arable EUR 17,212, irrigated olive EUR 25,245, huerta EUR 44,135, Canary banana EUR 281,808. USD figures at 1.125.

visas.name: Non-lucrative residence visa (visado de residencia no lucrativa)
visas.requirement: Passive income/savings of 400% IPREM = EUR 2,400/month (EUR 28,800/year) for the main applicant plus EUR 600/month (EUR 7,200/year) per dependent; IPREM frozen at EUR 600/month for 2026; full private health insurance with no co-pays; clean record. Must spend 183+ days/year in Spain to renew (enforced).
visas.initial_term: 1 year, renewals of 2 years + 2 years (RD 1155/2024 art. 64 keeps 2-year NLV renewals, not 4)
visas.processing_time: Typically 1-3 months at the consulate (legal maximum 3 months)

visas.name: Retiree route = non-lucrative visa (no separate pensioner visa)
visas.requirement: Same EUR 2,400/month (400% IPREM) test, satisfied with pension income; private insurance required at entry; after 12 months on the padrón you can buy into public healthcare via the convenio especial (EUR 60/month under 65, EUR 157/month 65+). Foreign pensions become taxable in Spain once resident.
visas.initial_term: 1 year, then 2 + 2 years

visas.name: Digital nomad / international teleworker visa (Ley 28/2022 'Startups Law')
visas.requirement: Remote employment or freelance income of 200% SMI = EUR 2,849/month in 2026 (SMI EUR 1,221 x 14 after RD 126/2026), +75% SMI for first dependent and +25% each additional; at least 80% of income from non-Spanish clients/employers; university degree or 3 years' experience; 3 months' relationship with the employer/clients. Can opt into the Beckham 24% flat-tax regime.
visas.initial_term: 1-year visa from a consulate, or 3-year residence permit if applied for in Spain; renewable for 2 years up to 5 years
visas.processing_time: About 20 working days via the Unidad de Grandes Empresas (UGE) when applied in Spain

visas.name: Self-employed residence and work permit (residencia por cuenta propia / autónomo)
visas.requirement: Viable business plan (a farm or farm co-op qualifies; no ENISA innovation test), proof of sufficient investment and funds for the project and your own upkeep, required qualifications/licences, clean record. No statutory minimum investment; plan is sized to the activity. Decision silence = refusal (art. 85 RD 1155/2024).
visas.initial_term: 1 year; renewals for 4 years under RD 1155/2024

visas.name: Entrepreneur visa (Ley 14/2013 art. 70, amended by Ley 28/2022)
visas.requirement: Innovative business plan of special economic interest endorsed by ENISA; funds adequate to the project (commonly EUR 10,000-50,000+); private insurance; clean record. Fits an agritech or regenerative-farming startup, not an ordinary farm.
visas.initial_term: 3 years, renewable for 2 years
visas.processing_time: About 20-30 days (UGE) when applied in Spain

visas.name: Employee residence and work permit (cuenta ajena)
visas.requirement: Job offer from a Spanish employer (a co-op or SL the group forms can sponsor) in a shortage occupation or after a labour-market test; full-time contract at SMI or above; RD 1155/2024 unifies residence and work authorisation.
visas.initial_term: 1 year; renewal 4 years
visas.processing_time: Up to 3 months plus consular visa time

visas.name: Arraigo (in-country regularisation: social, sociolaboral, socioformativo, familiar, segunda oportunidad)
visas.requirement: For people already living in Spain irregularly or whose permit lapsed: proof of a period of prior stay plus integration/job offer/training; all five routes authorise work since 20 May 2025; family arraigo gives 5-year permits. Not a route you can plan a move around, but it is the fallback for members who overstay.
visas.initial_term: 1 year (family arraigo 5 years)

visas.name: Citizenship by residence, reduced term for Ibero-Americans (Código Civil art. 22)
visas.requirement: Nationals by origin of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal or Sephardic origin qualify for citizenship after 2 years of legal residence (vs 10 years general, 5 for refugees); any residence permit above counts. The Ley de Memoria Democrática descendant window closed 22 Oct 2025.
visas.initial_term: n/a (naturalisation after 2 years' legal residence)

visa_text: Golden visa ENDED 2025; Non-Lucrative (€2,400/mo passive), Autónomo for farm co-op; citizenship 10y
visa_detail: Non-Lucrative (€2,400/mo passive, no work) or Autónomo (self-employed farm co-op). 1 yr →2+2. ~1–3 mo. PR 5 yr · citizenship 10 yr (2 yr for Ibero-Americans).
visa_note: Golden visa (Ley 14/2013 investor route) was abolished by Ley Orgánica 1/2025; last applications 3 April 2025. The Ley de Memoria Democrática 'Ley de Nietos' citizenship window closed 22 October 2025. New immigration regulation RD 1155/2024 in force since 20 May 2025: 1-year initial permits, 4-year renewals for work/self-employed permits, all arraigo routes now authorise work; the non-lucrative permit still renews for 2 years. EU/EEA/Swiss nationals need only register (certificado de registro) and are exempt from the military-zone land permit. 183+ days in Spain makes you tax resident on worldwide income.

tax.text: Income to ~47%; regional wealth tax (Andalucía ~0); Beckham 24% flat via nomad visa
tax.wealth_tax: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio 0.2%-3.5% on worldwide net assets above EUR 700,000 (plus EUR 300,000 main-home exemption); regions set their own scale and some (Madrid, Andalucía) bonify 100%, but the state Solidarity Tax on Large Fortunes (1.7% from EUR 3M, 2.1% from 5.35M, 3.5% above 10.7M) is now permanent and claws back the regional relief.
tax.property_tax: IBI: rural property 0.3-0.9% and urban 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value per year (cadastral values are well below market). Inheritance/gift tax 7.65-34% state scale, heavily reduced by most regions for close relatives.
tax.foreign_pension: Taxed as general income at 19-47% (state scale; combined regional scale varies) once you are resident; filing threshold EUR 22,000 from a single payer or EUR 15,000 from two or more payers; government/civil-service pensions are usually taxed only at source under treaties with exemption-with-progression in Spain.
tax.special_regime: Beckham regime (LIRPF art. 93): 24% flat on Spanish-source employment income up to EUR 600,000, 47% above, for the arrival year plus 5 more; open to digital-nomad-visa holders and qualifying freelancers since Ley 28/2022; requires no Spanish tax residence in the prior 5 years and Form 149 within 6 months of social-security registration. Foreign passive income is largely outside Spanish tax under the regime, but it does not help a farm co-op earning Spanish income.
tax.crypto: Crypto disposals and crypto-to-crypto swaps are savings income at 19-30%; staking/mining is general income; foreign-held crypto over EUR 50,000 reported on Modelo 721; DAC8 exchange reporting from 2026.
tax.coop_treatment: Ley 20/1990 on the tax regime of cooperatives: protected co-ops get a reduced corporate-tax rate on cooperative results (art. 33) and a 95% IAE bonification; 'especially protected' classes under art. 7 - worker co-ops, agrarian co-ops and cooperativas de explotación comunitaria de la tierra - get an additional 50% bonification of the corporate-tax liability (art. 34). Members are taxed personally on returns/wages.

cost.note: Small-town/rural Spain (Lugo, Jaén, Badajoz, Teruel, inland Andalucía) runs EUR 1,000-1,400/month per adult including a EUR 350-700 rental; groceries EUR 200-300; a car is effectively required. Excluding rent (owned commune housing) budget about EUR 650-900 (USD 730-1,010) per adult. Numbeo cost-of-living index 50.0 (Oct 2026).

health.system: Sistema Nacional de Salud (SNS): tax-funded, universal for residents, run by the 17 autonomous communities; Numbeo health-care index 76.8 (Oct 2026).
health.cost_for_residents: Free at point of use for insured residents; prescription co-pay 10-60% by income; private comprehensive insurance for visa purposes roughly EUR 50-200/month depending on age.
health.immigrant_access: Workers and autónomos (and their dependants) are covered automatically through social security. Non-lucrative visa holders must carry full private insurance (no co-pays, no waiting periods) at entry and renewal; after 12 months on the padrón they may join the public system via the convenio especial for EUR 60/month (under 65) or EUR 157/month (65+), which excludes subsidised prescriptions. Emergency care is open to everyone.
health.quality_note: Rural interior provinces have thin specialist coverage and long drives to hospitals; primary care (centro de salud) exists in most municipalities over ~1,000 people.

pension.text: Non-Lucrative visa; pensions taxed as income
pension.foreign_pension_tax: Once tax resident (183+ days) foreign private and state pensions are general income taxed at 19-47%; government-service pensions are generally taxed only in the paying state with exemption-with-progression; filing thresholds EUR 22,000 (one payer) / EUR 15,000 (two or more payers). No NHR-style pensioner regime exists.
pension.retiree_visa: No dedicated retiree visa; retirees use the non-lucrative visa (EUR 2,400/month or EUR 28,800/year passive income per applicant, EUR 600/month per dependent, 1 year then 2+2 renewals, no work).

ag.subsidies: CAP 2023-2027 via Spain's PEPAC: basic income support per eligible hectare (regionalised), eco-schemes, and for farmers under 40 a complementary young-farmer payment for up to 5 campaigns (+15% for women) plus regional establishment aid (intervention 6961.1, FEADER) typically capped at EUR 70,000-80,000 per new farmer. Access requires registering the holding (REGEPA/REA) and, for most schemes, being an 'active farmer' with the Spanish tax/social-security footprint a co-op or SAT provides.
ag.coop_law: Ley 27/1999 de Cooperativas (state) plus 16 regional co-op laws; cooperativas agrarias and de explotación comunitaria de la tierra (arts. 94-98) are the agricultural forms; Ley 20/1990 gives them 'especially protected' tax status. Sociedades Agrarias de Transformación (RD 1776/1981) are the lighter civil-society alternative.
ag.equipment_note: Investment aid for machinery, irrigation modernisation and processing comes through regional FEADER rural-development calls and is competitive; organic certification and young-farmer status improve scoring.

legal.text: Cooperativa de explotación comunitaria de la tierra — purpose-built communal land co-op

vehicles.name: Cooperativa de explotación comunitaria de la tierra (Ley 27/1999 arts. 94-98; regional equivalents)
vehicles.note: Purpose-built: members cede use rights over land/buildings to the co-op and may also contribute labour; the co-op farms it jointly. Minimum 3 members under state law; 'especially protected' under Ley 20/1990 art. 7 (50% corporate-tax bonification). Best fit for a commune that wants the land held and worked collectively while members keep title or cede it.

vehicles.name: Cooperativa de trabajo asociado / cooperativa agraria (Ley 27/1999)
vehicles.note: Worker co-op (members are the workforce, own the farm business and can own land) or agrarian co-op (members are farm holders pooling supply/marketing). Also especially protected for tax. Mondragón-style governance; one member one vote.

vehicles.name: Cooperativa de viviendas en cesión de uso (Ley 27/1999 art. 89; Catalan Ley 12/2015)
vehicles.note: Housing co-op where the co-op owns the dwellings and members hold indefinite use rights; the model used by Catalan cohousing and some ecovillages for the residential part, paired with an agrarian co-op for the farm.

vehicles.name: Sociedad Agraria de Transformación, SAT (RD 1776/1981)
vehicles.note: Civil society with legal personality for farming/forestry production and marketing; minimum 3 members, majority must be farm holders or farm workers, no member above one-third of capital; registered with MAPA/regional registry. Lighter than a co-op and widely used by family farms; fine for holding land and claiming CAP.

vehicles.name: Asociación (Ley Orgánica 1/2002 del Derecho de Asociación)
vehicles.note: Non-profit membership body that can own land and run community activities; no asset lock on dissolution unless written in; cannot distribute surplus. Used by several ecovillages as the umbrella for the community while a co-op or co-ownership holds the farm.

vehicles.name: Fundación (Ley 50/2002 de Fundaciones)
vehicles.note: Endowed non-profit with a permanent asset lock and government protectorate oversight; the closest Spanish equivalent to a community land trust for keeping land out of the market, but board-run rather than member-run and slower to set up.

vehicles.name: Comunidad de bienes / co-ownership (Código Civil arts. 392 ff.)
vehicles.note: Plain pro-indiviso co-ownership of one plot by all members with an internal agreement (Beneficio in Órgiva is held this way). Cheapest to create, but any co-owner can force a partition sale and shares pass to heirs, so it is fragile without a shareholders'-style pact.

vehicles.name: Sociedad Limitada, SL (RDL 1/2010 Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
vehicles.note: Standard limited company; can own land and employ members (which also opens the employee work-permit route). Taxed at the general corporate rate with none of the co-op bonifications; majority non-EU ownership does not avoid the military-zone permit.

vehicles.name: Community land trust (no Spanish statute)
vehicles.note: No CLT law; groups replicate it with a fundación or asociación holding title and a cesión-de-uso co-op or long leases (derecho de superficie, up to 99 years) for members' homes.

zoning.text: Foreigners CAN buy ag land; suelo rústico build ~1–2.5ha min; UMC anti-fragmentation
zoning.build_on_farmland: Agricultural land is 'suelo rústico/no urbanizable' under regional planning law. Only farm-linked buildings are generally permitted; a dwelling needs a large minimum parcel (Andalucía 2.5 ha for a non-farm isolated house with max 1% footprint, one house per parcel; Castilla y León from 5,000 m2 with UMC about 1 ha), setbacks and height limits, and municipal licence plus regional authorisation. Multiple homes for a group on one farm parcel are effectively impossible except by buying an existing hamlet/village nucleus with legal dwellings or a parcel already classed as urban/asentamiento. Rehabilitating existing ruins is the normal path.
zoning.communal_title: Freehold can be held by a co-op, SAT, asociación, fundación or SL, or by members pro indiviso (comunidad de bienes). UMC rules stop splitting the land into member-sized lots, which pushes groups toward a single entity holding title with internal use agreements.
zoning.note: Andalucía's Ley LISTA (2021) and its 2024-26 regulations tightened minimum parcels; check the municipal PGOU/PGOM before buying because local plans can be stricter than the regional floor.

climate.zone: Mediterranean on the east/south coasts, continental Mediterranean in the interior meseta (hot summers, cold winters, 300-500 mm rain), oceanic Atlantic in Galicia/Asturias/Cantabria/Basque Country (900-1,500 mm), semi-arid in Almería/Murcia.
climate.risks: Recurrent multi-year droughts and heatwaves, wildfire in the interior and north-west, flash floods on the Mediterranean coast; ND-GAIN 61.0 (rank 29) with low vulnerability (0.305) and decent readiness (0.525).
climate.water: The 2022-2024 drought broke after heavy late-2025 rain: reservoirs were about 77% full in July 2026 (10-year average 60%), Catalonia's internal basins 88%, but Murcia sat at about 30%. Irrigation rights (concesiones) are allocated by basin authorities and are scarce in the southeast; dryland and the Atlantic north are the safer bets for a water-independent farm.

life_text: High QoL, very safe; interior aging/thin
stab_text: Stable EU democracy, strong rule of law

stabWhy.pol: Stable EU parliamentary democracy with minority governments, recurring Catalan tension and a CPI slide to 55 (rank 49, down 10 points since 2012); FSI 44.0 'stable'.
stabWhy.law: WJP 2025 overall 0.71, rank 25/143 but only 18/31 in the EU/EFTA/North America group; courts independent, slow.
stabWhy.safe: GPI 2025 rank 25 (1.578); Numbeo safety 61.8; very low homicide, petty crime concentrated in cities.
stabWhy.econ: Eurozone member with euro stability; fast 2024-25 growth but structurally high unemployment and public debt; Numbeo purchasing power 107.
stabWhy.peace: GPI rank 25 of 163; EU/NATO member, no active conflict, ETA disbanded.
stabWhy.clim: ND-GAIN 61.0 (rank 29): low vulnerability but Spain is the EU's most drought- and desertification-exposed large country; 2022-24 drought only broke in 2025-26.

commune_history: Spain has one of Europe's deepest communal-land traditions: in 1936-37 anarchist peasants collectivised about 75% of the land in Republican Aragón (around 450 collectives federated at Caspe in February 1937) before the collectives were crushed, and since 1956 the Mondragón group has shown worker co-ops operating at industrial scale. The post-Franco wave began with Lakabe (1980), an abandoned Navarrese village reoccupied and later legalised, and Marinaleda, whose day-labourers won the 1,200 ha El Humoso estate in 1991 and run it through Marinaleda S.C.A. with EUR 15.52/month self-build housing. Today's live precedents are the Red Ibérica de Ecoaldeas (founded 1998, GEN-Europe member) and the statutory cooperativa de explotación comunitaria de la tierra in Ley 27/1999, which gives a new group a tested legal form rather than a workaround.
dealbreakers: Suelo rústico rules: you cannot legally build a cluster of homes on farmland (0.5-2.5 ha minimum per single farm-linked house, 1-2% footprint, regional authorisation), so a group must buy an existing aldea/village nucleus with legal dwellings or accept years of permitting.

Per-person visa money with no group route: EUR 2,400/month passive income per non-lucrative adult (no work allowed) or EUR 2,849/month foreign remote income per digital nomad, plus private insurance, every year until permanent residence at 5 years; the golden visa is closed.

Worldwide taxation after 183 days: 19-47% on income including foreign pensions, 19-30% on gains, wealth tax above EUR 700k and a permanent solidarity tax above EUR 3M; the Beckham 24% regime only helps remote employees, not a farm co-op.

Water: irrigation concessions are scarce in the south-east and droughts recur (2022-24 was severe); non-EU buyers also face a 2-6 month military-permit delay for rural land in coastal and border zones.
languages: Spanish (Castilian); co-official Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque, Aranese in their regions

corrections.new: ~8,100 USD/ha for typical dryland arable (MAPA 2024: tierras arables secano EUR 7,239/ha; national all-class average EUR 10,248/ha = USD 11,500); 4,000 only matches pasture (pastizal EUR 3,279/ha).

Griegos (Teruel) offered a family 3 months' free rent, then EUR 225/month (minus EUR 50 per school-age child) plus a job; no free plots. Other schemes: Ponga EUR 3,000 per couple + EUR 3,000 per child; Rubiá EUR 100-150/month aid.

True without restriction for EU/Swiss nationals and in the interior; non-EU nationals need Ministry of Defence authorisation (Ley 8/1975, RD 689/1978; 2-6 months) to buy rural land in the Balearics, Canaries, Ceuta/Melilla, French/Portuguese border strips, Galician and Cádiz coasts, Murcia and southern Alicante.
Range is 0.5-2.5 ha: Castilla y León permits a dwelling from 5,000 m2 (UMC ~1 ha); Andalucía's LISTA requires 2.5 ha for an isolated non-farm house with 1% max footprint and one house per parcel.

Regional 100% bonifications (Andalucía, Madrid) are overridden above EUR 3M by the state Solidarity Tax on Large Fortunes (1.7%-3.5%), which PwC now lists as permanent; below EUR 3M the regional relief holds.

corrections.old: Golden visa ENDED 2025; Non-Lucrative (€2,400/mo passive), Autónomo for farm co-op; citizenship 10y
corrections.new: Omits the digital nomad visa (Ley 28/2022), the main working route: EUR 2,849/month in 2026 (200% SMI after RD 126/2026), 3-year permit, Beckham-eligible; golden visa closed 3 April 2025 under Ley Orgánica 1/2025; self-employed permits now renew for 4 years (RD 1155/2024, in force 20 May 2025) while NLV renewals remain 2 years.
Add governance drift: CPI 2025 fell to 55 (rank 49), down 10 points since 2012 and now below the EU average; WJP 2025 0.71 ranks only 18/31 in its regional group.

verification.overall: The record is substantially accurate. Two numeric corrections: (1) farmland price 'typical' 8,100 USD/ha understates the MAPA 2024 national average of 10,248 EUR/ha (~11,900 USD/ha), with low and high ends also off; (2) the multiple-payer IRPF filing threshold is EUR 15,876, not EUR 15,000. All visa money thresholds (IPREM 600, SMI 1,221 x 14), RD 1155/2024 renewal periods, convenio especial fees, defence-zone rule, golden-visa closure, solidarity-tax permanence and the checked indices are confirmed. Rural cost of living and ND-GAIN/FSI values were not verifiable within budget. Publishable after applying the two corrections.

checks.claim: Foreign ownership of agricultural land 'allowed', with Ley 8/1975 / RD 689/1978 defence-zone military authorisation for non-EU buyers of rural land; SL >50% non-EU owned also caught; notary/registrar must demand the authorisation
checks.note: Art. 18 Ley 8/1975 requires prior military authorisation for acquisitions by non-EU foreign persons/companies in restricted zones; Spanish companies >50% non-EU owned are included; notaries and registrars must require proof before signing/registration. The 2-6 month processing time and the exact zone list are practitioner estimates, not verified against the primary text, but consistent with sources seen.

checks.claim: Farmland price typical 8,100 USD/ha (low 3,700, high 25,000)
checks.corrected_value: National average 10,248 EUR/ha in 2024 (~11,900 USD/ha); low ~5,100 EUR/ha (Castilla y León/Aragón rainfed cereal, ~5,900 USD); high 33,180 EUR/ha Murcia and 148,415 EUR/ha Canary Islands
checks.note: MAPA Encuesta de Precios de la Tierra 2024: average agricultural land 10,248 EUR/ha (+2.8%). The record's 'typical' 8,100 USD (~7,000 EUR) is ~30% below the official national mean; the low figure is also below the cheapest regional average, though individual secano/pasture parcels in interior regions can be cheaper. High end understates Murcia/Canarias.

checks.claim: Visa routes: NLV 400% IPREM = EUR 2,400/month + EUR 600 per dependent, IPREM EUR 600/month in 2026, 1y + 2y renewals (RD 1155/2024 art. 64), 183-day rule; DNV 200% SMI = EUR 2,849/month (SMI EUR 1,221 x 14 under RD 126/2026), 3-year permit in Spain; autónomo route 1y + 4y renewals, silence = refusal
checks.note: IPREM 2026 = EUR 600/month, NLV 400% = EUR 2,400/month + 100% IPREM per dependent confirmed. RD 1155/2024 art. 64: initial 1 year, renewal 2 years, and 64.2.f requires >183 days actual residence. RD 126/2026 sets SMI at EUR 1,221 x 14 (EUR 17,094/yr), so 200% = EUR 2,849/month. Autónomo 4-year renewal and art. 85 silence-refusal not separately verified.

checks.claim: Tax: worldwide taxation, top rate 47%, foreign pensions taxed at 19-47%, filing threshold EUR 22,000 single payer / EUR 15,000 multiple payers; Beckham 24% up to EUR 600k / 47% above for arrival year + 5
checks.corrected_value: Multiple-payer filing threshold is EUR 15,876 (tax year 2025, filed 2026), not EUR 15,000; single-payer EUR 22,000 is correct
checks.note: Agencia Tributaria IRPF 2025 manual: 22,000 EUR one payer; 15,876 EUR when second and subsequent payers exceed 1,500 EUR. The 15,000 figure is outdated (pre-2024). Top combined rate 47% and Beckham parameters are consistent with LIRPF art. 93 but were not re-fetched.

checks.claim: Monthly rural cost per adult 1,350 USD
checks.note: No authoritative rural-specific cost figure found; Numbeo publishes national single-person estimates excluding rent (~EUR 700-800) and rural rent varies widely. 1,350 USD (~EUR 1,160 incl. modest rent) is plausible but not verifiable.

checks.claim: Indices: GPI 2025 rank 25 / 1.578; WJP 2025 0.71; CPI 2025 55; HDI 0.918; Numbeo QoL 187.21, safety 61.82, healthcare 76.8; ND-GAIN 61; FSI 2025 44

checks.note: Ministry of Health and regional health services confirm the convenio especial (RD 576/2013): EUR 60/month under 65, EUR 157/month 65+, requires 1 year of padrón registration; pharmaceutical benefit not included.

Remaining coordinates are consistent with known village locations (Marinaleda, Valdepiélagos, Artieda, Órgiva area, Castilblanco area, Bierzo) but were not individually fetched.

checks.note: Golden visa abolished effective 3 April 2025 (LO 1/2025). Solidarity tax on net wealth >EUR 3M made indefinite from 2024 (via RDL 8/2023, not Ley 7/2024 as sometimes cited); rates 1.7-3.5%. Military authorisation rule confirmed via Ley 8/1975 art. 18. Suelo rústico minimum-parcel rules are regional and were not individually verified; EUR 700k wealth-tax state threshold is standard but regions vary (Madrid/Andalucía effectively zero).

name: Portugal
score_rationale: LAND 3: freehold for any foreigner, interior dryland EUR 1-5k/ha and listing average EUR 8.7k/ha, though subdivision is barred and prices doubled 2021-23. VISA 2: D7 at EUR 920/month is one of Europe's easiest entries, but citizenship is now 10 years, family reunification waits 2 years and AIMA is slow. TAX 2: no wealth tax, no inheritance tax for close family, crypto exempt after a year, negligible IMI on rustic land and cooperative exemptions, offset by a 48% (+5%) top rate and full progressive taxation of pensions for newcomers. LAW 2: excellent vehicles (cooperativa, associacao, baldios) but rustic/RAN land is effectively no-build and PDMs cap housing. LIFE 3: GPI 7th, HDI 0.890, Numbeo QoL 171.7, universal SNS. STAB 2: euro, A-rated, peaceful, but fragmented politics with a surging far right and acute wildfire/drought exposure keep it short of 3.
verdict: Cheap land, no foreign-ownership bar, surviving 10% pension regime — but the famous 5-year citizenship is now 10 and water is a risk.
summary: Portugal lets any foreigner buy rural land freehold, interior dryland still trades at roughly EUR 1,000-5,000/ha (listing average about EUR 8,700/ha) and the D7 passive-income permit needs only EUR 920/month per adult, so a group can get in cheaply and legally. The catches since 2025-26: naturalisation now takes 10 years (Lei Organica 1/2026), family reunification needs 2 years of prior residence (Lei 61/2025), new arrivals pay progressive tax (12.5-48% plus surcharge) on foreign pensions because the 10% NHR rate is closed, and rustic/RAN land is essentially no-build, so housing a group hinges on the municipal PDM. Use a cooperative (Lei 119/2015) or association to hold one undivided parcel, budget about USD 1,400/adult/month, and site away from the Centro/Norte wildfire belt.

land.text: Interior Alentejo/Beira farmland €7–11k/ha
land.house: No cash scheme; 'Aldeias' are heritage-tourism restoration
land.ownership_note: No nationality or residency condition on owning rural or agricultural land; EU and non-EU buyers purchase on the same footing as Portuguese nationals. You need a NIF (tax number), normally a Portuguese bank account, and a notarial deed; IMT transfer tax on rustic land is 5% plus 0.8% stamp duty. Constraints are land-use, not nationality: RAN (Reserva Agricola Nacional) and REN (ecological reserve) zoning, Natura 2000, and the 'unidade de cultura' minimum-parcel rule (Portaria 219/2016) that blocks splitting rustic plots (e.g. 24-48 ha for Alentejo dryland), so a group should buy one parcel into one entity. No lease or local-company workaround is needed.
land.build_rules: Rustic land cannot be subdivided below the 'unidade de cultura' (Portaria 219/2016; Alentejo dryland 24-48 ha depending on municipality, irrigated land far smaller). RAN land is non aedificandi under DL 73/2009 art. 20, with art. 22 exceptions (farmer's dwelling, agricultural support buildings) needing a DRAP opinion. Each municipal PDM sets its own minimum plot (commonly 1-4 ha+) for a single dwelling on rustic land. DL 117/2024 (in force 29 Jan 2025, four-year window) lets municipalities reclassify rustic land to urban only where 70% goes to public or cost-controlled housing, so it is not a tool for private communes.
land.cheap_house_program: No cash-for-houses or EUR 1 scheme. 'Aldeias Historicas/Aldeias de Xisto' are heritage-tourism restoration networks, not sale programmes. Depopulating interior municipalities (Beira Interior, Alto Alentejo, Tras-os-Montes) simply have very cheap ruins and rustic plots on the open market.
land.note: Price spread is huge: interior dryland (sequeiro) in Alentejo/Beira EUR 1,000-5,000/ha; the cocampo marketplace average across 751 listings is EUR 8,694/ha (Oct 2026); irrigated valley land in Beira (Vale da Vilarica EUR 21,000/ha, Cova da Beira EUR 35,000/ha by 2023) and Alqueva-perimeter olive/almond land reach EUR 30-45,000/ha; Eurostat's national average of EUR 76,556/ha (2024) is skewed by coastal, greenhouse and island land. Conversion at ECB rate 1.1225 USD/EUR (2 Oct 2026). Prices doubled 2021-2023 under investor demand.

visas.name: D7 Passive Income / Retirement Visa
visas.requirement: Regular passive income (pension, rent, dividends, interest, royalties) of at least EUR 920/month (100% of the 2026 minimum wage, EUR 11,040/yr) for the main applicant, +50% (EUR 460) for a spouse and +30% (EUR 276) per dependent child; savings of about one year's minimum wage (EUR 11,040); 12-month lease or property; NIF, Portuguese bank account, clean record, health insurance. Must spend at least 6 consecutive (8 total) months per year in Portugal.
visas.initial_term: 120-day entry visa, then 2-year residence permit, renewable for 3-year periods
visas.processing_time: Consulate 60-90 days plus AIMA card appointment 2-8 months depending on region (Faro about 2 months, Lisbon about 8); plan 6-9 months end to end

visas.name: D8 Digital Nomad (Remote Work) Visa
visas.requirement: Remote employment or freelance income from outside Portugal of at least EUR 3,680/month (4x minimum wage) shown over the prior 3-6 months, plus about EUR 11,040 savings; +50% of minimum wage (EUR 460) for a spouse; accommodation for 12 months. Residence-permit version gives the same 2+3 year track as D7.
visas.initial_term: 120-day entry visa, then 2-year residence permit, renewable for 3 years (a 1-year temporary-stay variant also exists)
visas.processing_time: Consulate about 60 days, AIMA 2-8 months; 6-9 months end to end

visas.name: D2 Entrepreneur / Independent Worker Visa (farm or cooperative founders)
visas.requirement: No fixed minimum investment; a viable business plan (a farm, cooperative or Lda counts), proof the business is incorporated or capital is available (lawyers commonly advise EUR 5,000+ share capital), and means of subsistence at least the minimum wage (EUR 920/month in 2026) plus family increments. AIMA assesses economic viability, so a group can incorporate one cooperative and have founding members apply individually.
visas.initial_term: 120-day entry visa, then 2-year residence permit, renewable for 3 years
visas.processing_time: Consulate 60-90 days plus AIMA 2-8 months; 6-10 months end to end

visas.name: Golden Visa (ARI) - investment fund and other non-real-estate routes
visas.requirement: EUR 500,000 in a CMVM-regulated non-real-estate fund (min 5-year maturity, 60% in Portugal-based companies), or EUR 500,000 in research or a company creating 5 jobs, or EUR 250,000 cultural donation (EUR 200,000 in low-density areas), or creating 10 jobs. Real-estate route abolished Oct 2023. Minimum stay only 7 days per year.
visas.initial_term: 2-year residence permit, renewable; investment must be held 5 years
visas.processing_time: 12-24 months to first card after AIMA digitisation (biometrics now 30-90 days), with historic backlogs of 3+ years

visas.name: Work visa (D1 employment contract / D3 highly qualified / EU Blue Card)
visas.requirement: Signed employment contract with a Portuguese employer (D1) or highly-qualified contract (D3). Since Lei 61/2025 (in force 23 Oct 2025) the 'manifestacao de interesse' in-country regularisation is gone and the job-seeker visa is limited to highly qualified workers, so entry must be arranged from the country of origin.
visas.initial_term: Entry visa then 2-year residence permit, renewable for 3 years

visas.name: CPLP residence permit (Brazil, Cape Verde, Angola, Mozambique, etc.)
visas.requirement: Nationals of CPLP states get a simplified residence permit, but after Lei 61/2025 they must obtain a consular visa first rather than regularising in-country. Naturalisation after 7 years (not 10) under Lei Organica 1/2026.
visas.initial_term: Residence permit renewable on the standard track

visas.name: Nationality by descent (children/grandchildren of Portuguese citizens)
visas.requirement: Children of a Portuguese citizen can register directly; grandchildren need effective ties to the national community and A2 Portuguese. No residence required. (Lei 37/81 as amended by Lei Organica 1/2026.)
visas.initial_term: Citizenship directly, no permit stage
visas.processing_time: Typically 1-2 years at the Conservatoria dos Registos Centrais

visa_text: Golden-visa RE route ended 2023 (fund/10-job remain); D7 passive, D2 entrepreneur; CITIZENSHIP now 10y (was 5)
visa_detail: D7 (~€920/mo passive), D2 entrepreneur, or golden-visa fund €500k. AIMA backlog 6–12 mo. PR 5 yr · citizenship now 10 yr (was 5, changed May 2026).
visa_note: Each adult in a group applies individually (couples/children as dependants); there is no group or community visa. D7 is the workhorse for anyone with EUR 920/month of documented passive income; D2 fits founders of the farm cooperative. Two 2025-26 changes matter for groups: Lei 61/2025 (23 Oct 2025) now requires the sponsor to hold 2 years of legal residence before family reunification, with housing, subsistence and Portuguese-language conditions; and Lei Organica 1/2026 (19 May 2026) raised naturalisation to 10 years of legal residence (7 for CPLP and EU nationals) with A2 Portuguese and a civics test, applications filed by 18 May 2026 staying under the old 5-year rule. Permanent residence still comes at 5 years. AIMA backlogs vary sharply by region (Faro about 2 months, Lisbon about 8).

tax.text: Income to 48%; crypto <1yr 28% else 0%; no wealth tax; 10% flat on foreign pensions survives
tax.capital_gains: Securities: 28% flat (or opt for progressive rates), with 50% inclusion for shares in unlisted micro/small companies and 10/20/30% exclusions for holdings of 2-5/5-8/8+ years; short-term gains must be aggregated with other income if taxable income exceeds EUR 86,634. Real estate: residents add 50% of the gain to progressive income; primary-residence gains exempt if reinvested in another EU home within 36 months, and a 2026-2029 exemption applies if reinvested in rental housing capped at EUR 2,300/month.
tax.wealth_tax: None (no net wealth tax); AIMI functions as a limited property-wealth surcharge above EUR 600,000 of residential urban value.
tax.property_tax: IMI annual tax on the tax value (VPT): rustic land 0.8%, urban buildings 0.3%-0.45% set by municipality (rustic VPTs are tiny, so a 20 ha dryland plot often pays under EUR 50/yr). AIMI surcharge of 0.7% (1% above EUR 1m) on residential urban property above EUR 600,000 per taxpayer (EUR 1.2m for jointly taxed couples). IMT on rustic land purchase 5%; stamp duty 0.8%. Inheritance/gifts: 10% stamp duty, but spouses, descendants and ascendants are exempt.
tax.foreign_pension: For anyone arriving now, foreign pensions are ordinary Category H income taxed at the progressive 12.5%-48% scale (2026 brackets: 12.5% to EUR 8,342 ... 48% above EUR 86,634) plus the 2.5%/5% solidarity surcharge above EUR 80,000/EUR 250,000. The 10% flat NHR pension rate survives only for people who obtained NHR before it closed (regime shut to new entrants from 2024; last transitional applications ended March 2025) and only for the rest of their 10-year window. IFICI (NHR 2.0) expressly excludes pensions. Treaty rules apply: e.g. foreign government-service pensions are often taxable only in the paying state.
tax.special_regime: IFICI / 'NHR 2.0' (from 2024): 20% flat tax for 10 years on Portuguese employment or self-employment income in listed qualifying activities (R&D, higher education, certified start-ups, export-oriented industry, certain highly-qualified roles) plus exemption of most foreign-source income, but NOT pensions. Requires not having been tax resident in the prior 5 years. Farmers, retirees and most commune members will not qualify; it is a professional-talent regime.
tax.crypto: Gains on crypto held under 365 days: 28% flat (Category G); held 365 days or more: exempt. Staking, lending and liquidity yield taxed at 28% as Category E income on receipt. Crypto-to-crypto swaps are disposals. Professional trading is business income at progressive rates.
tax.coop_treatment: Cooperatives are IRC (corporate tax) subjects, but agricultural, cultural, consumer, housing and social-solidarity cooperatives enjoy IRC exemptions on results from operations with their own members under Estatuto dos Beneficios Fiscais art. 66-A (results from third-party trade and non-cooperative activities remain taxed) - confirm scope with a Portuguese accountant; associations without profit motive are IRC-exempt on non-commercial income.

cost.note: About EUR 1,250 per adult: Numbeo's national single-person estimate is EUR 677/month excluding rent (2 Oct 2026) and a 1-bed outside the centre averages EUR 722 nationally (range EUR 500-1,140) but EUR 400-550 in interior towns such as Castelo Branco, Guarda, Beja or Portalegre; add about EUR 150 for a shared car and fuel, which are unavoidable in the interior. Members sharing community-owned housing and growing food can live on roughly EUR 800-900 (USD 900-1,000). Minimum wage is EUR 920 and local rural wages are low, so costs are far below Lisbon/Porto/Algarve.

health.text: SNS universal, co-pays gone; 1.56M lack family doctor
health.system: SNS (Servico Nacional de Saude): universal, tax-funded public system (Lei de Bases da Saude) with health centres (centros de saude/USF) in every municipality and public hospitals in district capitals; strong private sector (CUF, Luz, Lusiadas) used with EUR 50-150/month insurance. Numbeo Health Care Index 71.94 (Sep 2026).
health.cost_for_residents: Largely free at point of use: moderating fees (taxas moderadoras) were abolished for primary care, exams and referred emergency visits in 2022-2024; medicines are co-paid on a sliding scale; the SNS ran a deficit above EUR 1bn in 2025.
health.immigrant_access: Any legally resident foreigner - including D7, D8, D2, golden-visa, work and family-reunification permit holders - registers at the local health centre for a numero de utente with ID, NIF, address and the residence permit, and then has the same SNS rights as citizens. People without a residence permit after 90 days are seen only episodically and billed in full (except emergencies/communicable disease). Visa applicants must show private cover until the permit issues.
health.quality_note: Good hospital care but a chronic family-doctor shortage: 1,563,710 users had no assigned family doctor at end-December 2025 (up 2.7% on 2024; about 70% of them in Lisbon and Vale do Tejo), and 45% of GPs are over 65. Interior municipalities are often better covered for GPs but 1-2 hours from a hospital; expect to rely on a car.

pension.foreign_pension_tax: Progressive 12.5%-48% (plus 2.5%/5% solidarity surcharge above EUR 80k/EUR 250k) on worldwide pensions once tax resident (183 days or habitual home). The 10% flat NHR rate is closed to newcomers (NHR shut 2024, transitional window ended March 2025) and IFICI excludes pensions. US Social Security and most private pensions are taxable in Portugal under treaties; government-service pensions usually stay taxable at source.
pension.retiree_visa: D7 is the de facto retirement visa: EUR 920/month pension or other passive income per adult (2026), +50% for spouse, +30% per child, about EUR 11,040 savings; 2-year permit then 3-year renewals; PR at 5 years; citizenship at 10 years (Lei Organica 1/2026) with A2 Portuguese.

ag.subsidies: CAP via PEPAC 2023-2027. Young-farmer (18-40) first-installation premium: EUR 25,000 base + EUR 25,000 for full-time exclusivity + EUR 5,000 in 'vulnerable territory' = up to EUR 55,000 grant, plus co-financed productive investment up to EUR 400,000 (priority for mountain areas, rural job creation, trained applicants); 2025 call had EUR 143.6m. Any registered farmer with eligible hectares gets CAP basic income support and eco-schemes; organic conversion/maintenance payments and small-farm investment lines (C.2.2.1) exist. Foreign residents qualify once they hold a NIF, are registered as farmers (IFAP) and the holding is in the parcel register; group entities (cooperativa, Lda) can be beneficiaries.
ag.coop_law: Codigo Cooperativo, Lei 119/2015 of 31 Aug 2015 (amended by Lei 66/2017): minimum 3 members for a first-degree cooperative, variable capital, one member one vote, twelve branches including 'agricola' and multi-sector; agricultural cooperatives may admit investor members. Registered at the commercial registry; CASES (Cooperativa Antonio Sergio) issues the credential. CONFAGRI federates farm cooperatives.
ag.equipment_note: EU single market: any EU-spec tractor or tool imports duty-free; second-hand machinery market is thin in the interior; agricultural diesel (gasoleo colorido) and reduced 6% VAT on many inputs apply once registered as a farmer. Irrigation boreholes need APA licensing.

legal.text: Cooperativa (DL 335/99) coop-friendly; association; foundation

vehicles.name: Cooperativa (Codigo Cooperativo, Lei 119/2015, ramo agricola or multissectorial)
vehicles.note: Best fit: 3+ members, one-member-one-vote, variable capital, can own land and trade produce, eligible for PEPAC and for IRC exemptions on member business; Biovilla (Palmela) is a live example. Register with the commercial registry and CASES.

vehicles.name: Associacao sem fins lucrativos (Codigo Civil arts. 157-184; 'Associacao na Hora' fast-track)
vehicles.note: Cheapest and most common ecovillage form (Tamera and most GEN-Portugal projects use one): holds land, runs education/retreats, members cannot take profit or assets on exit, which protects the commons but blocks equity. Can be recognised as IPSS or 'utilidade publica' for tax perks.

vehicles.name: Fundacao privada (Lei-Quadro das Fundacoes, Lei 24/2012)
vehicles.note: Irrevocably endows land to a social purpose; needs government recognition and 'sufficient' endowment, heavy reporting. Suited to a mature group that wants the land permanently removed from the market, not to a start-up.

vehicles.name: Sociedade por quotas (Lda) / sociedade agricola
vehicles.note: Flexible, members hold quotas, can buy, farm and sell; supports D2 visa applications and bank finance; exits via quota transfer. Full IRC and no commons protection unless the articles add pre-emption and valuation caps.

vehicles.name: Baldios - community land (Lei 75/2017)
vehicles.note: Portugal's genuine commons: roughly 400,000 ha of inalienable village land in the north and centre run by assemblies of 'compartes'. Only residents of the local community can be compartes, so newcomers join by settling in the parish, not by buying; useful for grazing/forest partnerships rather than as a title vehicle. 2026 reforms end automatic co-management with the State.

vehicles.name: Compropriedade (co-ownership) with direito de superficie leases
vehicles.note: Simple joint title under the Civil Code; any co-owner can force a sale/partition and the unidade de cultura forbids physical splitting, so use only with a shareholders-style agreement, or hold title in a cooperative/association and grant members long surface rights (direito de superficie) for their houses - the closest Portuguese analogue to a community land trust.

zoning.text: Foreigners no restriction; RAN protects best soils (no-build)
zoning.build_on_farmland: Hard. Rustic land is non-building by default; RAN soils (DL 73/2009) are 'non aedificandi' except art. 22 exceptions (a farmer's dwelling tied to a viable holding, agricultural support buildings) with a DRAP opinion, and REN adds ecological no-build zones. The municipal PDM governs everything else and typically allows one single-family house per rustic parcel above a minimum (commonly 1-4 ha, sometimes 10+), so a 15-person community cannot legally build 15 homes on one farm without a PDM change or an 'empreendimento turistico'/rural-tourism licence. Wooden, mobile or 'yurt' housing still needs licensing. DL 117/2024 (in force 29 Jan 2025, four-year window) only lets municipalities reclassify rustic land where 70% is public or cost-controlled housing.
zoning.communal_title: Allowed and routine: title can sit in a cooperative, association, foundation or Lda, or in co-ownership. The unidade de cultura (Portaria 219/2016; 24-48 ha for Alentejo dryland, lower for irrigated land) prevents subdividing rustic land into member plots, which pushes groups toward one-entity ownership plus internal surface rights. Baldios are reserved to local resident communities.
zoning.note: Fire law (fuel-management strips around buildings, interior Centro/Norte are the most burned zones) and Natura 2000/Parque Natural overlays (e.g. Costa Vicentina, Arrabida) add further permitting layers. Tamera obtained accommodation through municipal planning over 30 years - plan for a multi-year dialogue with the camara municipal before buying.

climate.zone: Koppen Csa (hot-summer Mediterranean) south of the Tagus, in the inland Douro and interior Beira; Csb (warm-summer) north of the Tagus and on the Costa Vicentina. Interior Alentejo gets about 450 mm/yr, the Minho/Geres mountains up to 3,000 mm. Numbeo Climate Index 97.8 (very benign for people; demanding for dryland farming).
climate.risks: Wildfire is the headline risk: 2025 burned over 278,000 ha, the worst season since 2017, concentrated in Centro and Norte; by end-July 2026 another 53,700 ha had burned (third-worst since 2016). Multi-year droughts (2022-2024) triggered water restrictions in the Algarve and Alentejo; rising temperatures and longer heat waves are documented. ND-GAIN 62.8 (rank 24, low vulnerability/high readiness). Also winter storms (Jan-Feb 2026) and coastal/estuary flooding.
climate.water: Cyclical. After the wet 2025/26 hydrological year Alqueva stood at 84% (Aug 2026) with 6 bn m3 of inflow and Algarve reservoirs at 74%, yet APA still classed parts of the Alentejo as in drought. Irrigation outside the Alqueva perimeter depends on APA-licensed boreholes and farm ponds; Beira and the north are water-rich, interior Alentejo and the Algarve are not. Budget for rainwater storage and keyline works (Tamera's water-retention landscape is the local proof of concept).

life_text: #7 Global Peace Index; interior underdeveloped

stabWhy.pol: Stable democracy but a fragmented parliament: AD minority government after the May 2025 snap election with far-right Chega the second-largest party; moderate Socialist Antonio Jose Seguro won the Feb 2026 presidential run-off 66.8%-33.2% over Chega's Ventura.
stabWhy.law: WJP Rule of Law 2025 score 0.67 (rank 29, down one place); CPI 2025 score 56/100 (rank 46), eight points below the EU average and sliding; slow courts.
stabWhy.safe: Global Peace Index 2025 7th in the world (1.371); Numbeo Safety Index 66.65; violent crime rare in the interior.
stabWhy.econ: Euro member; S&P A+, Fitch upgraded to A+, Moody's A3; public debt falling from 89.7% of GDP (2025) toward 87% (2026) with a roughly balanced budget; growth about 1.7%; FSI 2024 25.9 (very sustainable).
stabWhy.peace: EU/NATO member, no internal or border conflict; GPI 7th.
stabWhy.clim: ND-GAIN 62.8 (rank 24) but the interior is Europe's most wildfire-exposed landscape (278,000+ ha burned in 2025) with recurrent drought in the Alentejo/Algarve.

commune_history: Portugal has two living traditions of communal land. The baldios - village commons in the north and centre, seized by the Estado Novo's forestry services and returned to their communities after 1974 (Lei 39/76, Lei 68/93, now Lei 75/2017) - are still run by assemblies of compartes and are the only land in Portugal that cannot be sold. In 1975 the Reforma Agraria saw landless workers occupy about 1.2 million ha of Alentejo and Ribatejo latifundios, organised into roughly 500 UCPs (Unidades Colectivas de Producao); the 1977 Lei Barreto and 1980s governments returned almost all of it, so that precedent is political memory rather than law. The modern precedent is the Codigo Cooperativo (Lei 119/2015) plus the association form: Tamera (Odemira, since 1995, about 250 people on 136 ha), Biovilla (a 2010 cooperative on 55 ha in Arrabida) and dozens of GEN-Portugal/RedeConvergir projects show that a foreign-founded community can hold land, be tolerated by the camara and, over time, obtain planning accommodation.
dealbreakers: Housing a group: rustic and RAN land is effectively no-build, PDMs usually allow one dwelling per large parcel, and the unidade de cultura forbids splitting the farm into member plots - many communes end up with unlicensed yurts and demolition orders.

Wildfire: 278,000+ ha burned in 2025 and the interior Centro/Norte (exactly where land is cheapest) is Europe's most fire-exposed landscape; insurance, fuel-management strips and evacuation planning are not optional.

A ten-year legal horizon: naturalisation is now 10 years (Lei Organica 1/2026), family reunification needs 2 years of prior residence (Lei 61/2025) and AIMA renewals can take months, so members must keep passive income or a business alive for a decade.
Pension-funded members lose the old 10% deal: foreign pensions are taxed at up to 48% + 5% for newcomers, which can cut a retiree's budget by a third compared with the pre-2024 NHR pitch.

corrections.new: The 10% flat rate survives only for people who obtained NHR before it closed (new entrants barred from 2024, transitional applications ended March 2025) and only for the remainder of their 10 years. New residents pay progressive 12.5%-48% plus 2.5%/5% solidarity on foreign pensions; IFICI (NHR 2.0) expressly excludes pensions.
D7 remains the retiree route, but foreign pensions are taxed at ordinary progressive rates (12.5%-48% + surcharge) for anyone arriving now.
The cooperative statute is the Codigo Cooperativo, Lei 119/2015 of 31 August 2015 (amended by Lei 66/2017), which replaced the 1996/1999 code; minimum 3 members for a first-degree cooperative.

Lei Organica 1/2026 (published 18 May, in force 19 May 2026): 10 years for most foreigners, 7 years for CPLP and EU nationals, with A2 Portuguese and a civic test; applications filed by 18 May 2026 stay under the 5-year rule.
