checks.note: 4,178 average and 9,707 (Colonia) high confirmed from DIEA-based reporting. The 2,300 low (Artigas) was not located in sources fetched; plausible but unverified.

checks.claim: Visa routes: rentista/pensionado ~USD 1,500/month single, ~2,500-3,000 couple; investor no fixed minimum; permanent residency granted directly; 12-24 months processing; citizenship 3/5 years; tax-holiday needs UI 12.5 M / USD 100k/yr fund / >183 days from 1 Jan 2026
checks.note: Spanish labour consejería states DNM requires a minimum of USD 1,500/month for rentista; practitioner sources give 12-24 months processing and USD 3,000 for families. Citizenship is 3 years with family in Uruguay, 5 without (record says 5y; fine as the conservative figure). 'Citizenship clock starts on filing date' not independently confirmed.

checks.claim: Tax system territorial, top personal rate 36%, foreign pensions not taxed; Ley 20.446 (16 Dec 2025) tax holiday: 11 years or 7% flat; routes >183 days / UI 12.5 M real estate / UI 625k/yr funds; post-holiday 6% for 5 years or UI 1.875 M fixed payment up to 20 years; old UI 3.5 M + 60-day route abolished for new entrants
checks.corrected_value: Ley 20.446 holiday: 11 years at 0% (IRNR option) for new residents from 1 Jan 2026 via >183 days, UI 12.5 M urban real estate bought from 2026, or UI 625k/yr funds. The 7% flat alternative closed permanently on 31 Dec 2025 and is NOT available to 2026+ entrants. Post-holiday: once-only 6% with UI 625k/yr funds or UI 6.25 M property; or fixed annual UI 1.875 M (reducible to UI 1.25 M with 183+ days or UI 45 M capital) for up to 20 years. The UI 3.5 M + 60-day test still creates tax residency; it simply no longer unlocks the holiday. From 2026 foreign capital gains are also taxable (12%). 36% top IRPF rate and foreign-pension exclusion confirmed.

checks.claim: Monthly rural cost per adult USD 1,300
checks.note: No source found either way within budget (search quota exhausted). Order of magnitude is consistent with the DNM USD 1,500/month solvency benchmark used for a single rentista.

checks.corrected_value: GPI 2025: 48th, 1.784 (GPI 2026 now 43rd, 1.754). WJP 2025: 0.72. CPI 2025: 73. HDI (HDR 2025): 0.862, rank 48. ND-GAIN: 56.6, rank 52. checks.note: All non-Numbeo values confirmed; FSI should be labelled 2024; Numbeo figures look like a live/2026 snapshot rather than the 2025 edition.

checks.claim: Healthcare: residents/applicants join ASSE free if income under 62 UR (+2.5 UR per family member) else paid cuota; FONASA contributors choose a mutualista with no monthly fee; direct mutualista USD 50-150/month
checks.note: gub.uy confirms the 62 UR + 2.5 UR/family-member free-affiliation threshold and that residency applicants (constancia de trámite) qualify; above-threshold households pay 'Cuota ASSE'. The USD 40-80 ASSE fee and USD 50-150 direct-mutualista ranges and the 'Mercosur simplified path' were not verified.

checks.claim: Communities exist, active, at stated coordinates: Comunidad del Sur, Colonia El Ombú, Gartental, Colonia Delta, Nueva Helvecia, Colonia Valdense
checks.note: El Ombú coordinates match Wikipedia (32°51′25″S 57°27′17″W). Colonia Delta (San José, ~97 km W of Montevideo near Ruta 1) and Gartental (NE Río Negro, ~65 km from El Ombú) consistent with stated coordinates. Comunidad del Sur confirmed active (Montevideo, Malvín Norte since 1964; sources also cite a 13-ha farm on Camino Maldonado km 16); no published coordinates, so the exact point -34.833,-56.117 is plausible but unverified. Nueva Helvecia and Colonia Valdense are well-known towns; not re-checked.

checks.note: Nuance: the rural minimum lot is 5 ha generally but 3 ha in Montevideo, Canelones, San José, Maldonado and Colonia (Ley 10.723 art. 16 as amended by 18.308), with exceptions down to 1 ha in delimited sectors. The '>183 days' requirement applies to the tax-holiday route, not to citizenship itself (citizenship needs habitual residence with no absence over 6 consecutive months). Drought 'worst in 74 years' and ~3% GDP (USD 1.88 bn, MGAP) confirmed.

name: Paraguay
score_rationale: LAND 3: freehold for foreigners, USD 500-2,200/ha Chaco and USD 1,500-5,000/ha eastern mixed land, property tax of a few dollars per hectare; only neighbour-country nationals face the 50 km border rule. VISA 3: still the easiest group route anywhere (no income threshold, about USD 390 state fee, PR at 2 years, citizenship 3 years later), kept at 3 despite 2026 tightening of solvency evidence and Interpol delays. TAX 3: territorial, 0% on foreign pensions/dividends/crypto, 8-10% on local income, no wealth or inheritance tax. LAW 3: Ley 438/94 cooperatives with tax-exempt member dealings, associations and foundations under the Civil Code, Ley 921/96 trusts, permissive rural building and a century-old Mennonite cooperative-colony precedent; caveats are the 20-member cooperative minimum, forest-reserve rules and title fraud. LIFE 2: Numbeo QoL 123 and healthcare 65 but safety 42, thin rural public health and few amenities outside Asunción and the colonies. STAB 1: CPI 24, WJP 0.45, FSI 61.5 and ND-GAIN 47.8 place it in the weak-institutions tier even though it is peaceful (GPI rank 75).
verdict: The strongest fit for the course's exact ask: cheapest land, easiest group residency, and a living Mennonite co-op precedent — if you accept weak institutions.
summary: Paraguay remains the cheapest, most open place in the Americas for a foreign group to buy freehold farmland and get residency: non-neighbour nationals buy rural land outright, Chaco land runs USD 500-2,200/ha and eastern productive land USD 1,500-5,000/ha, and temporary residency under Ley 6984/2022 needs no fixed income threshold (government fee about USD 390), converts to permanent after 2 years and to citizenship 3 years later. Taxes are territorial (0% on foreign pensions, dividends and offshore crypto gains; 8-10% on local income), and the Mennonite colonies show that cooperative land settlement works here. The trade-offs are weak courts and corruption (CPI 24, WJP 0.45), thin rural healthcare, drought/flood swings, and 2025-2026 tightening of residency paperwork (solvency evidence, Interpol checks).

land.text: Cheapest farmland in the Americas (Chaco $50–600/ha); foreigners own freely
land.ownership_note: Foreign individuals and foreign-owned companies hold rural land in full freehold with the same rights as Paraguayans; no permit, local company or nominee is needed and title passes by notarial deed registered at the Registro Público. The one structural limit is Ley 2532/2005, which bars nationals of the bordering countries (Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia) from owning rural land inside a 50 km border-security strip; US, EU, UK and other passport holders are not affected. Separately, agrarian-reform lots administered by INDERT (Estatuto Agrario Ley 1863/2002) cannot simply be bought from beneficiaries. Practical workaround for anyone caught by the border rule: buy outside the strip or hold through a Paraguayan company with a majority of non-neighbour owners (confirm with counsel). Title fraud and overlapping titles ('tierras malhabidas') are a real risk: insist on a cadastral survey (mensura) and a registry title search.
land.build_rules: No national minimum rural parcel size was found; subdivisions (loteamientos) and any construction need municipal approval under Ley 3966/2010. Rural properties over 20 ha in forest zones must keep 25% as native forest or reforest 5% (Ley 422/73 art. 42), and in the Eastern Region no forest may be cleared at all under the Zero Deforestation law 2524/2004 (extended to 2030).
land.cheap_house_program: None. Rural chacra land is cheap enough that most groups buy and build; municipal building permits are required under Ley 3966/2010 but are routine for farm dwellings.
land.note: Price tiers from 2025-2026 listings: Chaco cattle/forest land USD 500-1,500/ha (Presidente Hayes listings at USD 862-1,500/ha; Boquerón near Neuland USD 2,100-2,200/ha); eastern medium-quality mixed farmland USD 1,500-5,000/ha (San Pedro listings USD 4,360-4,750/ha); prime soy/corn land in Itapúa, Alto Paraná, Canindeyú USD 9,300-12,500/ha. Property tax is 1% of the fiscal value, which is a fraction of market value (2025 rural fiscal values Gs 1.54-3.39 million/ha east, Gs 0.16-0.96 million/ha Chaco), so annual tax is roughly USD 0.2-4.5 per hectare.

visas.name: Residencia Temporal (Ley 6984/2022) - general / self-employed route
visas.requirement: No fixed income or deposit threshold. Must show 'solvencia económica' with documents per the DNM annex (tightened by DNM Resolución 407/2026): employment contract, or RUC tax registration plus tax-compliance certificate for the self-employed, or apostilled professional degree, or dependent's support declaration. Apostilled birth and civil-status certificates, criminal records from origin country plus Interpol and Paraguayan police, two sworn declarations. Government fee Gs 2,926,925 (about USD 390) under Decreto 6225/2026 / Res. DNM 478/2026 from 1 July 2026; lawyers charge USD 3,000-6,000 extra. Must not be absent more than 12 consecutive months.
visas.initial_term: Up to 2 years, extendable for an equal period; in practice converted to permanent residency (10-year card) in months 21-24
visas.processing_time: 2-4 months for DNM approval; Interpol step slower since late 2025

visas.name: Residencia Temporal - retiree / pensioner (jubilado) category
visas.requirement: Same Ley 6984/2022 temporary residency; solvency is proven with an apostilled pension certificate. No minimum pension amount is set in law (the old 'USD 1,500/month' figure is not a legal requirement). Foreign pensions are untaxed under the territorial system. Same fee (Gs 2,926,925) and documents as the general route.
visas.initial_term: Up to 2 years, then permanent (10-year card)

visas.name: Residencia Temporal - employee (work contract) category
visas.requirement: Employment contract with a Paraguayan employer stating salary serves as solvency proof; employer registers worker with IPS (16.5% employer + 9% employee contributions). Same documents, fee and timeline as the general temporary residency.
visas.initial_term: Up to 2 years, then permanent

visas.name: Residencia Permanente por Inversión - SUACE productive track (Ley 6984/2022 art. 46; Res. 0283/2026)
visas.requirement: Minimum USD 70,000 invested through a Paraguayan company with a business plan, roughly 5 formal jobs and a 10-year deployment horizon (a farm enterprise qualifies). SUACE issues the investor certificate within 5 business days of a complete file; DNM then issues the permanent card. Resolución 0283/2026 (effective 28 April 2026) consolidated the investor tracks.
visas.initial_term: Permanent residency directly (10-year renewable card), skipping the temporary stage

visas.name: Paraguay Investor Pass - real estate / financial / tourism tracks (launched 17 April 2026)
visas.requirement: USD 200,000 in commercial real estate or in Paraguayan bank deposits/securities (2-year hold), or USD 150,000 in a SENATUR-registered tourism project; no company formation or job-creation requirement. Grants permanent residency directly; largely paperless with presence needed only for the cédula. Dividend tax for residents is 8% vs 15% for non-residents. Enabling law text was still being published as of spring 2026; maintenance conditions to be confirmed.
visas.initial_term: Permanent residency directly
visas.processing_time: Not yet officially published; SUACE certificate 5 business days, DNM card 4-10 weeks expected

visas.name: Residencia Temporaria MERCOSUR (Acuerdo de Residencia MERCOSUR)
visas.requirement: For nationals of Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru: passport/ID, birth certificate, criminal records; no solvency proof under the MERCOSUR agreement. Note Ley 2532/2005 still restricts Argentine, Brazilian and Bolivian nationals from rural land within 50 km of the border.
visas.initial_term: 2 years temporary, then permanent MERCOSUR residency

visas.name: Digital nomad / passive-income (no dedicated visa)
visas.requirement: Paraguay has no digital-nomad or rentista visa. Remote workers and passive-income holders use the general Residencia Temporal, proving solvency with foreign income/bank evidence (since Res. 407/2026 a diploma alone is not enough). Foreign-source salary, dividends and crypto gains are 0% taxed; most entrants also register a RUC.
visas.initial_term: Up to 2 years, then permanent

visa_text: Easiest in the world — no income proof, ~$350–1,400; PR 2y, citizenship 3y
visa_detail: EASIEST anywhere: temporary residence, NO income proof, ~$350–1,400, 60–90 days. PR after 2 yr · citizenship 3 yr.
visa_note: Group-friendly: each adult applies on the same dossier, minors are exempt from solvency proof, and there is no quota or sponsor. Naturalisation requires 3 years of effective permanent residency plus 'arraigo' (roughly 6 months/year presence, property or RUC ties), an A1-A2 Spanish/Guaraní interview and a 30-question civics test; Supreme Court processing adds 1-2 years. 2025-2026 changes: DNM Res. 407/2026 raised solvency evidence standards, Interpol checks now confirm with origin countries (delays), double-apostille rule for translated birth certificates, new fee schedule from 1 July 2026, and the Investor Pass / Res. 0283/2026 investor framework (April 2026).

tax.text: Territorial — 0% on foreign income/pension/crypto; 10% flat local
tax.capital_gains: Paraguay-source capital income (sale of local real estate, local dividends, interest) taxed at a flat 8% under IRP-RGC; gains on assets located abroad are untaxed. Residents receive local dividends with 8% IDU withholding (15% for non-residents).
tax.wealth_tax: None; no inheritance or gift tax either (PwC, reviewed Feb 2026).
tax.property_tax: Impuesto inmobiliario of 1% of the municipal fiscal value, adjusted yearly by CPI (+3.6% for 2025, +4.1% for 2026). Fiscal values are far below market: 2025 rural values Gs 1.54-3.39 million/ha in the Eastern Region and Gs 0.16-0.96 million/ha in the Chaco, i.e. roughly USD 0.2-4.5 per hectare per year.
tax.foreign_pension: Foreign pensions, foreign salaries for work performed abroad, foreign dividends and gains on foreign assets are outside the scope of IRP (0%) under the territorial principle (Ley 6380/2019, in force since 1 Jan 2020).
tax.special_regime: IRP is progressive on Paraguay-source personal-services income: 8% up to Gs 50 million, 9% to Gs 150 million, 10% above; filing exemption below Gs 80 million gross. Corporate IRE 10%; VAT 10% (5% on agricultural products and real-estate sales/rent). Ley 60/90 grants 100% customs-duty and VAT exemption on imported capital goods and machinery for approved investment projects; new investment law 7548/25 plus maquila 7547/25 adopted in 2025. Tax residency generally follows migratory residency and a RUC registration.
tax.crypto: Individuals pay 0% on gains from crypto traded on foreign exchanges (foreign source) and personal-asset sales fall outside IRE/IRP; a Paraguayan company selling crypto locally may owe 10% IRE. New in 2026: DNIT General Resolution 47/26 (March 2026) obliges residents and platforms to report crypto transactions above USD 5,000 per fiscal year (hashes, wallet addresses, origin/destination); further compliance phases are planned through 2026.
tax.coop_treatment: Cooperatives recognised under Ley 438/94 are exempt from income tax on acts between the cooperative and its members, and those member transactions are VAT-exempt (DNIT guidance); services to third parties are taxed normally.

cost.note: Numbeo (Sep 2026) puts a single person's costs excluding rent at about USD 556/month nationally (cost-of-living index 31, roughly 53% below the US); rural and small-town living with a modest rented room or own-built housing, local food and a motorbike runs USD 550-750 per adult. Expat guides quote USD 600-900 including rent for a comfortable single budget. Add USD 30-100/month for a local private health plan.

health.system: Three tiers: free public network run by the Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPBS); the contributory Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) for formal employees (16.5% employer + 9% employee payroll contributions, covering health and pension); and a private 'prepaga' market concentrated in Asunción, Ciudad del Este and Encarnación. Only about 31% of the population is insured (17.8% in rural areas).
health.cost_for_residents: Public: free. IPS: 25.5% of declared salary split employer/employee. Private local plan USD 30-100/month; international plans USD 300-800/month.
health.immigrant_access: MSPBS public hospitals and clinics treat anyone with valid ID, including tourists and temporary/permanent residents, free or near-free. IPS is tied to formal employment, so a commune would need to employ members through its cooperative/company to enrol them; self-employed foreign residents mostly cannot buy in and rely on private plans (USD 30-100/month local plans; consultations USD 20-50).
health.quality_note: Numbeo healthcare index 65 (driven by private Asunción hospitals). Public hospitals are underfunded and overcrowded, and rural posts lack specialists and medicines; the Mennonite colonies run their own well-regarded hospitals in Filadelfia and Loma Plata. Plan for 2-5 hour drives to serious care from most of the Chaco.

pension.foreign_pension_tax: 0%: foreign pensions are foreign-source income outside IRP under the territorial system; no wealth or inheritance tax. Retirees normally still register a RUC for banking.
pension.retiree_visa: No separate pensionado visa; retirees use Residencia Temporal (Ley 6984/2022) with an apostilled pension certificate as solvency proof, no minimum amount fixed in law, fee Gs 2,926,925 (about USD 390), permanent after 2 years, citizenship eligible 3 years later.

ag.text: Huge soy/cattle co-ops; Mennonite model proven
ag.subsidies: Little direct EU-style subsidy. The state bank Crédito Agrícola de Habilitación (CAH) lends at subsidised rates to small producers and cooperatives (44,737 families, Gs 529.6 billion in credits July 2024-June 2025); the Ministry of Agriculture (MAG) runs family-agriculture technical assistance and input programs. Ley 60/90 gives approved investment projects 100% exemption from customs duties and VAT on imported capital goods and machinery; agricultural machinery imports remain tax-exempt. Soy, maize and beef exports are the backbone and large cooperatives (Chortitzer, Fernheim, Neuland, Colonias Unidas) dominate processing and marketing.
ag.coop_law: Ley 438/94 de Cooperativas (regulated by Decreto 14052/96, amended by Ley 5501/15): minimum 20 members aged 18+, recognised and supervised by INCOOP; cooperatives are private legal persons of social interest and member transactions are exempt from income tax and VAT. Agrarian cooperatives may own land, run processing plants, credit unions and clinics, as the Mennonite colonies do.
ag.equipment_note: Machinery and inputs are imported duty-free (Ley 60/90 and current machinery exemptions); used equipment and parts are widely available through the Mennonite cooperatives in Filadelfia/Loma Plata and Brazilian dealers in Alto Paraná. Expect to drill wells or build 'tajamares' (rain ponds) in the Chaco, where groundwater is saline.

legal.text: Ley de Cooperativas 438/94; LIVING MENNONITE CO-OP precedent (1.8M ha)

vehicles.name: Cooperativa (Ley 438/94, Decreto 14052/96, Ley 5501/15)
vehicles.note: Best fit for a producing commune: democratic one-member-one-vote, can own land and run farm, store, credit and clinic; member transactions tax-exempt. Needs 20 adult members and INCOOP recognition, so small groups must start as a company or association and convert.

vehicles.name: Asociación civil sin fines de lucro (Código Civil Ley 1183/85, arts. 91 ff.)
vehicles.note: Non-profit membership body formed by public deed; 'asociación reconocida de utilidad pública' (executive decree) has full capacity, 'asociación inscripta de capacidad restringida' is simpler. Can hold land and run the community; the 2024 NGO-control law adds registration and reporting duties that the IACHR flagged.

vehicles.name: Fundación (Código Civil Ley 1183/85)
vehicles.note: Asset-locked purpose entity without members; useful as a land-steward holding title in perpetuity (closest native analogue to a community land trust) with the farm operated by a cooperative or company that leases from it.

vehicles.name: Fideicomiso (Ley 921/96 de Negocios Fiduciarios)
vehicles.note: Statutory trust where a BCP-supervised fiduciary (bank or financial entity) holds land for named beneficiaries; good for succession and anti-partition protection but adds fiduciary fees and bank oversight.

vehicles.name: SRL / SA / EAS (Empresa por Acciones Simplificada, Ley 6480/2019)
vehicles.note: Fastest route for foreigners and the vehicle for SUACE investor residency; EAS can be formed online with one shareholder. Holds land cleanly but is not democratic by default; dividends face 8% IDU. Needed if any member is an Argentine/Brazilian/Bolivian national buying near the border.

vehicles.name: Condominio (co-ownership under the Civil Code)
vehicles.note: Simple joint title in several names; cheapest but any co-owner can force partition or sale and heirs inherit shares, so only suitable as a stop-gap before forming a cooperative or foundation.

vehicles.name: Comunidad indígena title (Ley 904/81 Estatuto de las Comunidades Indígenas)
vehicles.note: The only true communal, inalienable, indivisible land title in Paraguayan law, but granted free by the state solely to recognised indigenous communities; not available to settler groups.

zoning.text: Foreigners own rural land freely (except 50km border strip)
zoning.build_on_farmland: Yes. Rural land has no agricultural-only zoning; dwellings, workshops and farm buildings on a chacra need only a municipal building permit and plan approval under Ley 3966/2010 (Orgánica Municipal), and rural land is expected to be put to productive use under the Estatuto Agrario (Ley 1863/2002). Environmental constraints bite instead: no clearing of native forest in the Eastern Region (Ley 2524/2004 'Deforestación Cero', extended to 2030), a 25% native-forest reserve on rural properties over 20 ha in forest zones or 5% reforestation (Ley 422/73 art. 42), and MADES environmental licensing for land-use change.
zoning.communal_title: No communal title exists for non-indigenous groups; land is held by a cooperative, association, foundation, company, trust or in co-ownership. Indigenous communities alone hold inalienable collective title under Ley 904/81.
zoning.note: INDERT agrarian-reform parcels carry transfer restrictions and should be avoided; check that any cheap eastern lot is not an unregularised 'asentamiento'. Off-grid building is common; ANDE grid connection is cheap where lines exist.

climate.zone: Humid subtropical (Köppen Cfa) in the Eastern Region with 1,400-2,000 mm rain, hot summers (35-40 C), mild winters with occasional frost; tropical savanna to hot semi-arid (Aw/BSh) in the Chaco, 1,000 mm at its eastern edge falling to 400-600 mm in the far west.
climate.risks: Alternating drought and flood driven by ENSO: severe droughts 2008-09, 2012-13 and 2020-22 (Chaco worst hit), river floods on the Paraguay/Paraná and Pilcomayo (April 2025 central-Chaco flood affected about 8,500 families), heat waves with high humidity, Chaco wildfires and occasional freezes. Projected warming of about 2 C by 2050; the 2025 World Bank CCDR flags intensifying drought. ND-GAIN 47.8 (rank 88).
climate.water: Eastern Region: abundant good-quality surface water and large aquifers (Guaraní system) with strong recharge; Central/Western Chaco: surface water scarce, seasonal and salty, groundwater fossil and saline, so settlements depend on rainwater harvesting into tajamares and cisterns.

life_text: Cheap, quiet; modest amenities

stabWhy.pol: Electoral democracy with peaceful transfers but near-continuous Colorado party dominance and clientelism; FSI 61.5 (Finland 14.3, Turkey 84.0).
stabWhy.law: WJP Rule of Law 0.45 (100/143, down 1% in 2025) and CPI 24/100 (150/182): courts slow and politicised, land-title fraud common.
stabWhy.safe: Numbeo safety index 42; rural interior calm but eastern-border narco routes and the small EPP insurgency in the north-east keep GPI societal-safety scores middling.
stabWhy.econ: Stable guaraní, low public debt, 10% flat-ish taxes and territorial system; commodity-driven (soy/beef) with drought-sensitive growth and a large informal economy.
stabWhy.peace: GPI 2025 score 1.981, rank 75 and 4th in South America; no interstate conflict, landlocked buffer state.
stabWhy.clim: ND-GAIN 47.8 (rank 88): high exposure to drought/flood cycles and heat, limited adaptive capacity, better in the humid east than the Chaco.

commune_history: Paraguay has courted communal settlers for 140 years: Nueva Germania (1887), William Lane's socialist Nueva Australia and Cosme colonies (1893-94, land granted by the state and later dissolved into individual lots), and above all Ley 514 of 26 July 1921, the Mennonite 'Privilegium', which gave pacifist colonists military exemption, German schools and tariff-free imports and underpins the Menno (1926), Fernheim (1930) and Neuland (1947) cooperative colonies that today run dairies, meatpacking and hospitals across the central Chaco. The Bruderhof's Primavera colony (1941-1961, three villages near Itacurubí del Rosario) showed that a fully communal, multi-national Christian commune could be hosted, and the Bruderhof returned to Asunción in 2010 (Villa Primavera). The live precedent is the Raiffeisen-style cooperative under Ley 438/94: a group that buys land, forms a cooperative and runs production, credit and services through it is following a model the state and banks already understand.
dealbreakers: Land-title fraud and overlapping 'tierras malhabidas' titles: buying without a registry search and cadastral survey can mean losing the farm in slow, corruptible courts (WJP 0.45, CPI 24).

Water and climate in the Chaco: saline groundwater, 400-1,000 mm erratic rain, multi-year droughts (2020-22) and flash floods (April 2025) make cheap Chaco land unworkable without large rain-harvesting investment; the humid east is safer but costs 3-10x more.
Thin rural healthcare and services: public hospitals are underfunded, IPS is closed to most self-employed foreigners, and serious care means hours of travel to Asunción or the Mennonite hospitals.

Residency paperwork is tightening (2025-2026 solvency rules, Interpol confirmations, apostille demands) and the cooperative form needs 20 adult members, so a small group must plan a company/association interim structure and keep every member's absences under 12 months during the temporary stage.
languages: Spanish and Guaraní (both official); Plautdietsch/German in Mennonite colonies; Portuguese common on the eastern border; little English outside Asunción.
currency: Paraguayan guaraní (PYG); approx. 7,500 PYG per USD used for conversions in this record
